title_ar: الشيخ الددو في استضافة قناة دليل حول موضوع تمثيل ومحاكاة الشخصيات الإسلامية
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Hosted by the Dalil Channel on the Subject of Acting and Representing Islamic Figures
body_ar:
استضافت قناة دليل صباح أمس الجمعة الموافق لـ 29/07/2011 فضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء في برنامج " البيان التالي"، في حلقة تناقش موضوع: "تمثيل وتجسيد الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم في الأعمال الدرامية للقنوات التلفزيونية".

وكانت هذه الحلقة من البرنامج حلقة مثيرة للكثير من النقاش ظل مطروحا منذ فترة على المنظور الشرعي وأثارت ردودا متباينة بين العلماء أنفسهم وبين الرأي العام في المجتمع الإسلامي والعلماء من جهة أخرى.

تناولت هذه الحلقة مع الشيخ الددو الإجابة الشرعية على تساؤلات يطرحها المحاور والمتدخلون في البرنامج، واتسمت هذه الحلقة بشكل عام بإبراز الموقف الشرعي من التمثيل والمحاكاة معتمدا في ذلك على الأصول الشرعية من الكتاب والسنة والاستنباط الشرعي من الأصول وفق قواعد الأصول المعروفة من مراعاة المصالح والمفاسد والقياس وتغير الفتوى وسد الذرائع ...

وضمن الأسئلة التي أجاب الشيخ عنها في هذا الحوار ما يلي: - هل تجسيد الصحابة فعل جائز ؟. – ما هي الشروط التي يضعها المجيزون والمانعون لهذا الفعل؟. - ما الفرق بين تقمص الشخصية وبين ترسيخها وتثبيتها من لدن المحاكي في النظر الشرعي؟؟.

كما تخللت هذه الحلقة من البرنامج محاورات ومناقشات مع بعض العلماء والمتدخلين في البرنامج.

وخلال مناقشة هذا الموضوع أبرز الشيخ الددو أن أصل التمثيل يختلف حكمه باختلاف هدفه؛ فإذا قُصد بالتمثيل السخرية أو الطعن في الأشخاص أو أهداف أخرى غير مقبولة شرعا كترسيخ الطائفية أو الفتن فهو ممنوع شرعا.

أما إذا كان تمثيل الصحابة يُقصد به أمر تعليمي محض يخدم ترسيخ النصوص وإثبات التاريخ الصحيح للأمة فهو أمر جائز. ونبه في هذا السياق إلى التمييز بين تمثيل وتجسيد الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم وتمثيل الرسل والأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم وسلامه، فالمانع من تجسيد الأنبياء والرسل ليس مانعا شرعيا وإنما هو مانع أدبي وأخلاقي لأن التمثيل لا يمكنه أن يأتي بحقيقة أوصافهم الكريمة وشمائلهم العظيمة.

وشدد الشيخ الددو بهذا الصدد على ضرورة مراعاة فقه الفتوى والواقع المتغير للأمة.

ومما استدل به الشيخ في حديثه من أن أصل المشروعية في هذا التمثيل ما حكاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحابه عن نبي من الأنبياء دمّاه قومه وضربوه فجعل يمسح الدم عن وجهه هكذا ( ويفعل بيده) ويقول: "يا رب اغفر لقومي فإنهم لا يعلمون"، وذكر أن ما كان من هذا التمثيل على وجه السخرية فهو ممنوع شرعا لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما حكت عنده عائشة رضي الله عنها رجلا أنكر ذلك.

وضمن المواضيع الشائكة التي نوقشت في هذا الحوار ما يتعلق بالفرق بين تقمص الشخصية وبين ترسيخ الصفة وتثبيتها من لدن الممثل أو المحاكي، وما أثير حول فِلم الحسن والحسين، وأما مسالة إنفاق الأموال في إنتاج هذه الأفلام فهي مسالة ذكر الشيخ أنها لم تُطرح للرأي الفقهي ولو طرحت عليه لكان الجواب في نظره أن الأولى بها أن تنفق على ما هو أهم من هذه الأفلام والبرامج، كالمجاعة في الصومال ووحدة الصف المسلم.

لمتابعة هذه الحلقة إضغط هنا.
body_en:
The Dalil channel hosted His Eminence the learned Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, on the morning of yesterday, Friday 29/07/2011, on the programme "The following statement", in an episode discussing the subject: "The acting and embodiment of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, in the dramatic productions of the television channels".

This episode of the programme was one that stirred a great deal of the discussion that has been going on for some time from the standpoint of the Sharia, and it provoked divergent responses among the scholars themselves, and between public opinion in Muslim society on the one hand and the scholars on the other.

This episode with Sheikh al-Dedew took up the answer from the Sharia to questions put by the interviewer and by those contributing to the programme. In general the episode was marked by its setting out the position of the Sharia on acting and representation, relying in this on the foundations of the Sharia in the Book and the sunnah, and on the derivation of rulings from the sources according to the known rules of legal theory: regard for benefits and harms (maṣāliḥ and mafāsid), analogical reasoning (qiyās), the change of a considered legal opinion (fatwā) with circumstances, and blocking the means to harm (sadd al-dharāʾiʿ)…

Among the questions the Sheikh answered in this exchange were the following: Is the embodiment of the Companions a permissible (jāʾiz) act? What are the conditions laid down for this act by those who permit it and by those who forbid it? What, in the view of the Sharia, is the difference between an imitator's taking on a personality and his fixing and entrenching it?

The episode was also interspersed with exchanges and discussions with some of the scholars and with contributors to the programme.

In the course of discussing this subject Sheikh al-Dedew brought out that the ruling on acting as such differs according to the difference in its aim: if what is intended by the acting is mockery, or the impugning of persons, or other aims not acceptable in the Sharia, such as the entrenching of sectarianism or of discord, then it is prohibited in the Sharia (mamnūʿ sharʿan).

But if what is intended by the acting of the Companions is a purely instructional matter, serving to fix the texts and to establish the community's correct history, then it is a permissible (jāʾiz) matter. In this connection he drew attention to the distinction between the acting and embodiment of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, and the acting of the messengers and prophets, God's blessings and peace be upon them: for what prevents the embodiment of the prophets and messengers is not an impediment of the Sharia but a literary and moral impediment, because acting cannot bring across the reality of their noble attributes and their great qualities.

In this regard Sheikh al-Dedew stressed the necessity of taking into account the jurisprudence of issuing legal opinions and the changing circumstances of the community.

Among what the Sheikh adduced in his talk, that the basis of legitimacy in such acting is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, related to his Companions about one of the prophets whom his people bloodied and beat, so that he began to wipe the blood from his face like this (and he would act it out with his hand) and to say: "Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know." And he mentioned that whatever of such acting is done by way of mockery is prohibited in the Sharia (mamnūʿ sharʿan), because when ʿA'ishah, may God be pleased with her, mimicked a man in the Prophet's presence, may God bless him and grant him peace, he rebuked that.

Among the thorny subjects discussed in this exchange was what bears on the difference between an actor's or imitator's taking on a personality and his fixing and entrenching the trait, and what has been raised concerning the film al-Hasan and al-Husayn. As for the question of spending money on producing such films, the Sheikh mentioned that it had not been put for a juristic opinion, and that had it been put to him, the answer in his view would be that it is more fitting for that money to be spent on what is more important than these films and programmes — such as the famine in Somalia and the unity of the Muslim ranks.

flags.context: فإذا قُصد بالتمثيل السخرية أو الطعن في الأشخاص … فهو ممنوع شرعا
options: prohibited in the Sharia (mamnūʿ sharʿan) — the source's own word, kept
flags.note: CRITICAL for the five-rulings mapping. The word in the source is ممنوع, not حرام. ممنوع is the news desk's ordinary word for 'not allowed' and does not by itself identify which of the five rulings the Sheikh gave: a jurist may say ممنوع of something he holds ḥarām, and also of something he holds makrūh or barred on grounds of blocking the means to harm (sadd al-dharāʾiʿ), which the same paragraph lists among the principles he used. Rendering it 'forbidden (ḥarām)' would put a ruling in his mouth that this record does not establish. The Arabic word is therefore carried across with its transliteration and the reader can see that it is not one of the five terms. Which ruling he actually gave has to be taken from the recording.

flags.arabic: هل تجسيد الصحابة فعل جائز ؟ / فهو أمر جائز
flags.context: the question put to him, and his answer on instructional portrayal
flags.note: The kalām exemption of style guide section 8 does not apply here. جائز attaches to an act (the portrayal of the Companions), not to a proposition about God, so it takes the ordinary legal sense of the five-rulings table and is rendered 'permissible'. Recorded explicitly because جائز is one of the terms the addendum singles out as easy to mistranslate, and this record is one where the wrong sense would be nonsense.

flags.context: a news desk summary of a televised discussion on a contested contemporary question
options: display with a prominent caveat that this is a journalist's summary and that the ruling is in the recording
flags.note: CRITICAL — critical_for_display. This is the record in this span most likely to be mistaken for a fatwa. It states positions in ruling language on a live and disputed question — whether the Companions may be portrayed by actors — and it does so in two lines each way, with the conditions that the permitting and forbidding scholars attach named as a question but never answered. The Sheikh gave a reasoned answer over the course of a television programme; what survives here is a précis. It must not be rendered as a fatwa, and a reader must be told where the answer actually is: the recording at /index.php/fiker-islam.html?view=media&id=1488.

flags.arabic: وما أثير حول فِلم الحسن والحسين
options: render the title literally, as done here, with no gloss
add a gloss identifying the drama series
flags.note: A reference to a television drama on al-Hasan and al-Husayn that was controversial at the time and that lies behind the whole discussion, including the mention of 'entrenching sectarianism' earlier in the record. No gloss has been inserted, because identifying the production and its backers would add a context the Arabic does not supply and would sharpen a sectarian edge the record leaves implicit. A reviewer may wish to supply an editorial footnote kept visibly separate from the report.

flags.arabic: ما حكاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم … عن نبي من الأنبياء دمّاه قومه / لما حكت عنده عائشة رضي الله عنها رجلا أنكر ذلك
flags.context: the two prophetic reports the Sheikh is said to have adduced
options: translate and attribute exactly as given, with no collection and no grading
flags.note: Style guide section 4. Neither report is given a collection or a grading in the source, so the English supplies neither. Both are load-bearing here — the first is offered as the very basis of legitimacy for representational acting and the second as the basis of the prohibition on mockery — so a reviewing scholar will want to check both against the recording before the record is displayed.

translator_notes: This is a news report on a television programme, written by the site's news desk. Every ruling in it is a journalist's summary of what the Sheikh said on air. Nothing in it is a written text by him.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body dates the broadcast to the morning of Friday 29 July 2011.

تمثيل is rendered 'acting' and تجسيد 'embodiment' throughout, and محاكاة 'representation' or 'imitation' according to context. The three are kept distinct because the record turns on the difference between them.

فقه الفتوى والواقع is rendered 'the jurisprudence of issuing legal opinions and the changing circumstances of the community' rather than left as a formula. It is a modern term of art and is not in the glossary.
The source's closing line 'to follow this episode click here' is the site's navigation furniture; preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, omitted from body_en.
